claims.text: Thermal aging at 400 °C enhances local chemical order at grain boundaries in duplex or stainless steels.
Enhanced grain-boundary chemical order stabilizes and improves the uniformity of the passive oxide film.
A more stable and uniform passive oxide film increases corrosion resistance.
As-received duplex or stainless steels have typical grain-boundary Cr and Ni distributions.
Isothermal annealing at 400 °C for 1 to 24 hours can promote local chemical order without inducing deleterious phase precipitation.
The proposed controlled study should compare as-received samples with samples aged at 400 °C for 1, 6, 12, and 24 hours.
Samples should be tested in acidified chloride solutions using potentiodynamic polarization and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy.
TEM/EDS should be used to characterize passive films and grain-boundary chemistry.
Aging produces grain-boundary regions with increased local chemical order and optimized Cr, and possibly Ni, segregation.
Enhanced local chemical order reduces the mobility of vacancies and defects at grain boundaries.
Reduced vacancy and defect mobility at grain boundaries fosters formation of a continuous, chemically uniform passive oxide film.
A continuous, chemically uniform passive oxide film is more resistant to localized breakdown and corrosion propagation.
Aged specimens will have higher breakdown potentials than as-received controls.
Aged specimens will have lower corrosion current densities than as-received controls.
Aged specimens will exhibit more uniform Cr-enriched passive films at grain boundaries than as-received controls.
As-received steels have less uniform passive films and lower corrosion resistance than appropriately aged steels.
The proposed mechanism should apply only when aging does not cause significant secondary-phase precipitation or embrittlement.
The optimal aging duration is uncertain because prolonged aging may trigger adverse phase changes.
Variability in microstructural responses may reduce reproducibility.

The hypothesis is falsified if aging produces no statistically significant improvement in breakdown potential and corrosion current density, or no enhancement in Cr segregation and passive-film uniformity relative to the as-received baseline.
